Name: Grain Origination Management
Definition: The ability to attract, contract and secure grain from growers and member cooperatives.

Name: Grower Relationship Management
Definition: The ability to establish and keep relationships with growers who sell grain directly to CHS.

Name: Purchase Contract Management
Definition: The ability to offer, maintain and price grain purchase commitments with growers and cooperatives.

Name: Member Cooperative Supply Management
Definition: The ability to secure, contract and coordinate grain supply from independent member cooperatives.

Name: Grain Handling and Storage Management
Definition: The ability to receive, assess, store, account for and load grain at CHS facilities.

Name: Inbound Grain Receiving
Definition: The ability to accept, identify and weigh inbound grain.

Name: Inventory Control
Definition: The ability to know the quantity, quality and ownership of grain in storage.

Name: Outbound Grain Loading
Definition: The ability to load grain into trucks, railcars and barges to schedule and specification.

Name: Grain Merchandising and Risk Management
Definition: The ability to price, position, sell and hedge grain and oilseed commitments profitably.

Name: Basis Management
Definition: The ability to value, set and manage the local cash-to-futures price relationship.

Name: Location Basis Valuation
Definition: The ability to value basis by location and period, including freight spreads and carry.

Name: Basis Exposure Management
Definition: The ability to measure and limit open basis risk against approved limits.

Name: Spread and Carry Management
Definition: The ability to manage time spreads and storage carry to decide when to hold or sell grain.

Name: Futures and Options Risk Management
Definition: The ability to offset price risk using exchange-traded futures and options.

Name: Transportation and Network Logistics Management
Definition: The ability to plan, secure and manage freight and the shape of the facility network.

Name: Rail Logistics
Definition: The ability to secure, use and track rail capacity for grain shipments.

Name: Rail Capacity Procurement
Definition: The ability to secure shuttle and railcar capacity from railroads on usable terms.

Name: Railcar Utilization Management
Definition: The ability to maximize trips per shuttle set and minimize idle cars and penalties.

Name: Rail Shipment Visibility
Definition: The ability to know where rail shipments are and when they will arrive.

Name: Freight Performance Management
Definition: The ability to measure and improve freight cost, carrier performance and penalties.

Name: Supply Network Design
Definition: The ability to decide where facilities, capacity and grain flows should be in the network.

Name: Grain Processing and Product Conversion
Definition: The ability to convert soybeans into oil, meal, hulls and refined oil products.

Name: Oilseed Processing
Definition: The ability to convert soybeans into crude oil, meal and hulls.

Name: Crush Capacity Management
Definition: The ability to plan and balance crush volume across Fairmont and Mankato.

Name: Crude Soybean Oil Production
Definition: The ability to extract crude soybean oil to specification.

Name: Soybean Meal and Hull Production
Definition: The ability to produce meal and hulls to feed-market specifications.

Name: Food Ingredient Production
Definition: The ability to refine crude soybean oil into food-grade and specialty oil products.

Name: Market Distribution and Customer Fulfillment
Definition: The ability to deliver grain and products to domestic and export customers as committed.

Name: Export Market Fulfillment
Definition: The ability to meet export sales commitments from Minnesota origins.
